settings.themeHelp: System matches your device light or dark mode. Turn on System colors to use the platform palette in the app (including Material You on Android). Buttons and accents follow your phone’s primary color so the app matches your wallpaper when dynamic color is available.
settings.clockFormatHelp: Automatic follows your device's own clock setting. Prayer times, the month table and your widgets all use the same format.
settings.systemDynamicColorsHelp: Uses your device’s semantic and dynamic colors in the app when theme is System. Pure black (OLED) still darkens backgrounds when dark mode is on.
settings.pureBlackHelp: True black background in dark mode for OLED displays.
settings.providerAutoHelp: In Sweden, prayer times use the Sweden source (listed cities); outside Sweden, AlAdhan. Pick a source below to lock one provider.
settings.providerOverridden: {{picked}} has no times for where you are, so {{used}} is answering instead.
settings.manualSearchHelp: Tap a search result to apply it right away, or edit coordinates and press Apply below.
settings.calcHiddenSweden: Sweden uses prayer times per listed city. Your position is reverse-geocoded to match that city; only for Sweden.
settings.calcHiddenPraytimes: PrayTimes.dev applies its own published rules (see prayertimes.dev). Only madhab / Asr school applies here; method list is hidden.
settings.prayerAlertsHelp: Scheduled for the five daily prayers (Fajr–Isha). Android may require exact-alarm access for reliable timing.
settings.prePrayerReminderHelp: Optional second notification before each prayer.
settings.liveActivityHelp: Pinned countdown to the next prayer, with today's other times in the expanded view.
settings.liveActivityCompactHelp: Show only the countdown; hide the prayer list.
settings.languageHelp: Select the app language. Arabic and Urdu use right-to-left layout.
settings.widgetConfigureHint: You can also touch and hold the widget → settings (gear) to adjust the same options on Android.
settings.adhanAlarmStreamHelp: Uses the alarm volume, so the adhan is heard even when the phone is on silent or vibrate. Does not override Do Not Disturb.
settings.notificationSoundDefaultHelp: Uses your device default notification sound.
settings.notificationSoundVoiceHelp: Built-in voice included in this app build.
settings.notificationSoundCustomHelp: Choose an audio file from this device.
settings.notificationSoundCustomTrimmed: Notifications play the first 30 seconds; the full recording plays when the app is open.
settings.prayerOffsetsHelp: Nudge each prayer by ±{{max}} minutes to match your local mosque.
settings.attributionsBlurb: Whose work this app is made of
settings.accentColorHelp: Used across the app and the home-screen widget.
settings.widgetColorFollowsAccentHelp: The widget uses the same accent color as the app. Pick it under Appearance.
settings.widgetColorOwnHelp: The app is following your system colors, which the widget does not. Pick the widget’s highlight here.
settings.additionalTimesBlurb: Sunrise, midnight and the thirds of the night
settings.additionalTimesFooter: These appear in the prayer table, the widget and the Live Activity as well as in notifications, and they use the default sound rather than the adhan.
settings.dailyRemindersBlurb: An ayah each day, and today's khatmah portion
settings.sunriseTimeHelp: Show sunrise in the prayer table, notifications, widget, and Live Activity.
settings.islamicMidnightHelp: The midpoint of the night between Maghrib and Fajr. Off by default.
settings.lastThirdHelp: The start of the last third of the night — the time for Qiyam al-Layl. Off by default.
settings.firstThirdHelp: The end of the first third of the night — in the Maliki reckoning, where Isha leaves its preferred window. Off by default.
settings.malikiSecondTimesHelp: Each prayer gets a line on the Today card saying when its preferred time (ikhtiyari) closes and its late time (daruri) begins. Computed on your device from your coordinates, whichever source your times come from. Uses the 1:1 shadow for Asr regardless of your madhab setting, because that is the Maliki boundary. Off by default.
settings.malikiSecondTimesHanafiWarning: Heads up: these are Maliki boundaries, but your Asr is set to Hanafi, which uses a different shadow. Zuhr's first time will end about half an hour before the Asr shown below it. Turn off Hanafi Asr if you want the card to agree with itself.
settings.malikiSecondTimesSource: From Al-Murshid al-Muin (Ibn Ashir), as rendered in The Guiding Helper, Song 11.
settings.malikiAlertsHelp: Off for every prayer to begin with. Pick only the ones you want to be told about — five more alerts a day is how an app teaches you to ignore it. Needs notifications turned on.
settings.malikiAlertsLeadTitle: Warn me before the first time ends
settings.malikiSecondTimesModelled: Fajr's and Asr's boundaries are the stars fading and the sun yellowing — an angle standing in for something the eye judges. They are marked as approximate. Where the sun does not rise, does not set, or never reaches the angle, nothing is shown rather than a guess.
settings.rateAppHelp: Enjoying the app? A rating helps others find it.
settings.ayahOfDayHelp: A randomly chosen ayah with its translation, every day.
settings.khatmahReminderHelp: Today's portion and where to continue, while a khatmah is active.
settings.khatmahReminderNoPlan: Start a khatmah in the Qur’an tab to use this.
settings.resetAppHelp: Erase all settings and data. Cannot be undone.
settings.batteryWarningHelp: Battery optimization can delay or silence adhan alerts while the app is closed. Tap to exclude Mihrab.
settings.themeRestartManualBody: iOS does not allow apps to restart themselves. Please force-quit Prayer Times and reopen it for the new theme to take effect.
settings.liquidGlassHelp: Adopt iOS system colours and translucent glass chrome. Follows Light/Dark automatically.
settings.themeRestartBody: Switching system colors needs the app to restart so every screen picks up the new theme. Restart now?
settings.laLockButtonHelp: Show a button on the card for hiding it from the lock screen and always-on display.
settings.resetBody: This wipes all settings, saved locations, journal entries, fasting log, and tasbih state, then takes you back to the onboarding flow. This cannot be undone.
settings.endOfDayLogHelp: Ten minutes after Isha, asks whether to log the day’s five prayers. Answering it the next morning still logs the right day.
settings.alertModeHint: Changes how this prayer alerts you
settings.sectionNotificationsBlurb: Sounds, advance reminders, extra times, live activity
settings.sectionLocationBlurb: Where you are, and your saved places
settings.malikiRows: Show them in the day’s times
settings.malikiRowsHelp: Off, the boundaries are only announced — nothing is added to the card or the month.
settings.malikiEndAlertsHelp: A second notification at the moment the prayer becomes qada. Fired at the time itself, never early.

compass.needLocationBody: Set a location in Settings or open Home once with GPS so we can compute the Qibla direction.
compass.hint: Hold the phone flat and move away from metal. Align the Qibla arrow with “Phone front” when you face the Qibla.
compass.signalHelp: Based on magnetic field level and stability. Move away from metal and electronics if it stays low.
compass.signalWeakBody: Move away from metal, magnets, and electronics. Remove magnetic phone accessories, then make a slow figure-8 motion to recalibrate.
compass.motionDetectedBody: Too much movement can make direction jump. Hold the phone flat and still for a few seconds, away from moving vehicles or speakers.
compass.motionPermissionDeniedBody: Compass access is denied on iOS. Allow Motion & Fitness access in system settings, then reopen this screen.
compass.unsupportedBody: This device does not provide a usable magnetometer (or access failed). The live compass is turned off. Use the bearing below with a physical compass or map.
compass.checkingCompassWithPrompt: Starting compass… If prompted on iOS, allow Motion & Fitness access.
compass.a11yDialLive: Qibla compass. Rotate {{deg}} degrees to face Qibla.
compass.a11yDialChecking: Qibla compass. Waiting for sensor data.
compass.a11ySignal_weak: Compass signal: weak. Try moving to an open area.
compass.a11ySignal_very_weak: Compass signal: very weak. Accuracy may be limited.
compass.crossCheckBody: Your device's own compass is tuned to its hardware. For the most accurate reading, open it and turn until it shows {{degrees}}.

sync.pairIntro: Sync keeps your record the same on every device you use. Mihrab never moves anything itself: it needs a folder that Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, Syncthing or similar already keeps in step between your devices. Mihrab writes one small encrypted file there, and only your own devices can read it.
sync.thisDeviceHelp: Show this code to your other device, or type it in there. It is not a password — it is safe to copy, photograph or send to yourself.
sync.addDeviceHelp: Type or paste the code shown on your other device.
sync.pairWarnBody: Everything recorded on that device will appear here, and everything here will appear there. Merging never deletes: where the two disagree, the more recent entry is kept.
sync.pairedBody: This device has written its key to the folder. Open Mihrab on the other device — as soon as it reads the folder, both are paired and syncing.
sync.errorBadCode: Check the code and try again. It is grouped in sixes, and a single wrong character is enough to reject it.
sync.errorThisDevice: That is this device’s own code. You need the one shown on the other device.
sync.errorTooMany: You can pair up to {{max}} devices. Remove one first.
sync.errorSaveBody: The device wouldn’t store it. Try again — nothing was changed.
sync.removeBody: This device will stop sending to it and stop accepting from it. Remove this device on that one too, or it will keep trying.
sync.notReady: This device can’t set up sync: it has no secure source of randomness, and a key made without one would not be private.
sync.privacyNoteP2p: Your code is a public key, not a secret. The data itself is encrypted for your paired devices only, and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
sync.folderHelp: Choose a folder your sync service already keeps in step on every device — a Nextcloud, OneDrive, Dropbox or Syncthing folder. If nothing is syncing that folder between your devices, nothing will reach them. Mihrab writes one small encrypted file there and reads the ones your other devices left.
sync.autoHelp: Automatic syncs run only while the app is open. Sync now always works, whatever you choose here.
sync.errorFolderGone: That folder can’t be reached any more. Choose it again.
sync.errorUnsupported: This build can’t use folder sync.
sync.syncDoneBody: Everything your other devices had is here now, and what is here is there.
sync.syncNothing: Nothing new. Your other devices haven’t written anything since the last check.

hint.quranTitle: Reading on more than one device?
hint.quranBody: Set up sync and your place, bookmarks and khatmah follow you between them.
hint.logTitle: Log on one device, see it on all of them
hint.logBody: Set up sync to keep your record the same everywhere. Nothing is uploaded.

sync.pairedNeedsFolder: Choose a folder first. That folder is how the two devices reach each other, and until there is one, nothing can be exchanged.
sync.folderAppHint: Mihrab made a folder called {{value}} for itself. Find it in Files, under On My iPhone, and point your sync app at it to reach your other devices.
sync.syncNothingArrived: Your file is in the folder, but nothing from your other devices has appeared there. Both devices have to be pointing at the same folder, and whatever keeps that folder in step between them has to be running.
sync.syncStale: Your file is in the folder, but the newest record from {{device}} was written {{when}}. If you have used that device since, whatever keeps the folder in step between you has stopped carrying files.
sync.scanHint: Point the camera at the code on your other device
sync.scanDeniedBody: Mihrab needs the camera to read the code. You can allow it in your device settings, or type the code in instead.
sync.scanNoCameraBody: This device has no camera to scan with. Type or paste the code instead.
sync.errorFolderUnwritable: That folder can’t be written to. Pick another one — a folder you made yourself in Documents or Downloads works best.

stats.owedHint: Tap a day to make it up
